Haplotype blocks of target loci

Source: R/hgsi-blocks.R
hbr_haplotype_blocks.Rd

Groups a set of target loci into haplotype blocks by one of seven methods and reports the block assignment. Two calling conventions are supported.

Usage

hbr_haplotype_blocks(
  plink_prefix = NULL,
  units = NULL,
  cm_snp = NULL,
  chr_snp = NULL,
  method = c("recomb", "ld", "either", "fourgamete", "gabriel", "recomb+gabriel",
    "recomb+fourgamete"),
  flank_cM = 1,
  max_snps = 400L,
  max_span_cM = 5,
  min_gamete = 0.01,
  maf_min = 0.05,
  rmax = 0.01,
  r2 = 0.5,
  ld_max_cM = 3,
  r2_min = 0.25,
  gabriel_grid = 21L,
  carry = NULL,
  genetic_map = NULL,
  cM_per_Mb = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

plink_prefix

PLINK prefix, or an `hbr_run` object (in which case the run-level API is used). When the first positional argument is an `hbr_run`, this argument receives it.

units

Low-level API: data.frame with `chr` and `cm` per target locus, and `snp_col` when using the SNP-level methods. Alternatively, an `hbr_run` object (in which case the run-level API is used).

cm_snp, chr_snp

Low-level API: genetic positions and chromosomes of every SNP in the PLINK file.

method

One of the seven methods above.

flank_cM, max_snps, min_gamete

SNP-level methods only: window around the genes, SNPs kept per cluster, and gamete frequency that counts as recombination.

max_span_cM

Largest distance between the first and last locus of a block.

maf_min

Minimum minor-allele frequency.

rmax

Maximum Haldane recombination fraction between neighbours for `"recomb"`.

r2

Minimum carrier-indicator r-squared for `"ld"`.

ld_max_cM

Largest distance over which LD may join neighbours.

r2_min, gabriel_grid, carry

Reserved for future versions; kept for backward compatibility with the low-level API.

genetic_map, cM_per_Mb

Genetic positions for the run-level API: a data.frame with `chr`, `bp`, `cm` (for example [hbr_rice_genetic_map()]), or a constant rate. A `.bim` with an informative cM column is used when neither is supplied.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

For the low-level API, an integer vector of block IDs per row of `units`. For the run-level API, an object of class `hbr_blocks` with elements `blocks`, `units`, `lines`, `full`, `snp_clusters`, `settings` and `map_source`.

Details

**Low-level.** Supply `plink_prefix`, `units`, `cm_snp` and `chr_snp` directly. `units` must carry `chr`, `cm` and (for the SNP-level methods) `snp_col`; `cm_snp` and `chr_snp` give the genetic and physical position of every SNP in the PLINK file. The function returns an integer vector of block IDs per row of `units`. This is the legacy API and is fully backward compatible.

**Run-level.** Pass an `hbr_run` (from [hbr_read_results()]) as the first positional argument or as `plink_prefix`. The function reads the superior haplotypes, rebuilds the codes, replays the discovery gate to pick the best haplotype per gene, places each at its genetic map position, and returns a classed `hbr_blocks` object with the block table, the per-line carrier matrix, and (for SNP-level methods) the SNP windows used.

The seven block methods are:

`"recomb"`

Join neighbours whose Haldane recombination fraction is at most `rmax`. Describes the recombination expected in a new cross.

`"ld"`

Join neighbours whose carrier indicators have r-squared at least `r2` within `ld_max_cM`. Describes LD in the panel.

`"either"`

Union of `"recomb"` and `"ld"`.

`"fourgamete"`

Four-gamete rule on the SNPs around the genes (Wang et al. 2002; Haploview default).

`"gabriel"`

Gabriel-type D-prime confidence intervals (Gabriel et al. 2002).

`"recomb+gabriel"`

Union of `"recomb"` and `"gabriel"`, then capped at `max_span_cM`.

`"recomb+fourgamete"`

Union of `"recomb"` and `"fourgamete"`, then capped.

Blocks never span chromosomes. `"recomb"`, `"ld"` and `"either"` operate on the loci directly; the SNP-level methods read a window of `flank_cM` around each cluster of target genes.

See also

[hbr_read_results()] to build the run input, [hbr_haplotype_block_table()] for the legacy low-level wrapper.

Examples

# Legacy low-level API — no genotypes needed for the map methods
units <- data.frame(chr = c("1", "1", "1", "2", "2"),
                    cm  = c(10, 10.5, 50, 5, 5.2))
hbr_haplotype_blocks(method = "recomb", units = units)
#> [1] 1 1 2 3 3

# Run-level API on the bundled toy data
toy <- system.file("extdata", "hgsi_toy", package = "HaploBreedR")
if (nzchar(toy) && dir.exists(toy) &&
    requireNamespace("BEDMatrix", quietly = TRUE)) {
  run <- hbr_read_results(file.path(toy, "trait_YLD"))
  blk <- hbr_haplotype_blocks(
    run, plink_prefix = file.path(toy, "geno_toy"),
    method = "recomb")
  blk$blocks
}
#>   using bundled rice genetic map (Harushima 1998 / RGP); pass `genetic_map = "none"` to disable
#>   block chr start_cM end_cM n_target_haplotypes n_genes  genes traits
#> 1 HB001   2      0.0    0.0                   1       1 GENE04    YLD
#> 2 HB002   3      1.1    1.1                   1       1 GENE07    YLD
#>   panel_freq
#> 1     0.1667
#> 2     0.3333
